idea: Place the refined Erdős–Soifer block at a non-aligned position: let the (m+1)×(m+1) fine grid straddle cell boundaries, offset by a fraction of a cell. Re-solve the neighbouring coarse cells with the compaction LP so partially covered cells become rectangles re-tiled by equal squares. This generates (Δcount, Δsum) pairs, including even count changes, that aligned replacements cannot give.
